title: Relationship of Anthropometric and Training Characteristics with Race Performance in Endurance and Ultra-Endurance Athletes
authors: Beat Knechtle
abstract: Anthropometric and training characteristics were analyzed for their relationship with race performance in endurance and ultra-endurance athletes. Key predictors for ultra-endurance performance included fast shorter-race times, low body fat, and high training speed.

title: Effects of ascorbic acid supplementation on oxidative stress markers in healthy women following a single bout of exercise
authors: Manita Yimcharoen, Suwatsin Kittikunnathum, Chawannut Suknikorn, Wichuda Nak-on, Petcharee Yeethong,...
abstract: This study investigated ascorbic acid's effects on oxidative stress markers in women after exercise. Ascorbic acid improved antioxidant capacity but did not prevent exercise-induced muscle damage.

title: Marginal vitamin C status is associated with reduced fat oxidation during submaximal exercise in young adults
authors: Carol S Johnston, Corinne Corte, Pamela D Swan
abstract: Marginal vitamin C status was studied in relation to fat oxidation during submaximal exercise. Low vitamin C status was associated with reduced fat oxidation, which was improved by vitamin C repletion.

title: Effects of Running-Specific Strength Training, Endurance Training, and Concurrent Training on Recreational Endurance Athletes’ Performance and Selected Anthropometric Parameters
authors: Pablo Prieto-González, Jaromir Sedlacek
source: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
abstract: This study investigated the effects of running-specific strength, endurance, and concurrent training on recreational runners. Concurrent training demonstrated the most comprehensive improvements in body composition and performance metrics.

title: Effects of Separate Cognitive Training on Endurance Exercise Performance
authors: Neil Dallaway, Steven R. Bray, Kira L. Innes, Kathryn E. Andrusko, Christopher Ring
source: Journal of Functional Morphology and Kinesiology
abstract: This study investigated the impact of standalone cognitive training on endurance exercise. Results showed no improvement in endurance performance, perceived exertion, or heart rate compared to control groups.

title: Vitamin C may alleviate exercise-induced bronchoconstriction: a meta-analysis
authors: Harri Hemilä
abstract: This meta-analysis examined if vitamin C affects exercise-induced bronchoconstriction. Vitamin C administration significantly reduced post-exercise FEV1 decline and the proportion of participants experiencing EIB.

title: Strength Training Prior to Endurance Exercise: Impact on the Neuromuscular System, Endurance Performance and Cardiorespiratory Responses
authors: Matheus Conceição, Eduardo Lusa Cadore, Miriam González-Izal, Mikel Izquierdo, Giane Veiga Liedtke, ...
abstract: This study examined strength training's acute effects on neuromuscular and cardiorespiratory responses during endurance exercise. Strength training before endurance exercise impaired time-to-exhaustion, with no significant changes in oxygen uptake or heart rate.

title: Antioxidants and Exercise Performance: With a Focus on Vitamin E and C Supplementation
authors: Madalyn Riley Higgins, Azimeh Izadi, Mojtaba Kaviani
abstract: This paper reviews antioxidant supplementation, specifically vitamins E and C, for exercise performance. Evidence suggests supplementation may hinder exercise adaptations and is generally not beneficial, except in specific circumstances.

title: Influence of Vitamin C Supplementation on Oxidative Stress and Neutrophil Inflammatory Response in Acute and Regular Exercise
authors: Ljiljana M. Popovic, Nebojsa R. Mitic, Dijana Miric, Boban Bisevac, Mirjana Miric, Brankica Popovic
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C's impact on oxidative stress and neutrophil inflammation from exercise. Vitamin C supplementation reduced exercise-induced lipid peroxidation but did not affect neutrophil inflammatory response.

title: Differences in Training Adaptations of Endurance Performance during Combined Strength and Endurance Training in a 6-Month Crisis Management Operation
authors: Kai Pihlainen, Keijo Häkkinen, Matti Santtila, Jani Raitanen, Heikki Kyröläinen
source: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
abstract: This study compared training adaptations in soldiers during a 6-month operation. Soldiers who were initially leaner and fitter were more likely to experience a decrease in aerobic fitness.

title: Does Vitamin C and E Supplementation Impair the Favorable Adaptations of Regular Exercise?
authors: Michalis G. Nikolaidis, Chad M. Kerksick, Manfred Lamprecht, Steven R. McAnulty
abstract: This study investigated whether vitamin C and E supplementation interferes with exercise adaptations. High doses of these vitamins are not recommended for exercising individuals due to conflicting evidence on their efficacy and potential harm.

title: Training for a (half‐)marathon: Training volume and longest endurance run related to performance and running injuries
authors: Tryntsje Fokkema, Ankie A.D.N. van Damme, Maarten W.J. Fornerod, Robert‐Jan de Vos, Sita M.A. Bierma...
source: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
abstract: Training volume and longest endurance runs were studied in relation to marathon performance and injuries. Higher training volumes and longer endurance runs were associated with faster finish times, without an increased risk of injury.

title: Effects of Heavy Strength Training on Running Performance and Determinants of Running Performance in Female Endurance Athletes
authors: Olav Vikmoen, Truls Raastad, Olivier Seynnes, Kristoffer Bergstrøm, Stian Ellefsen, Bent R. Rønnesta...
abstract: This study examined the impact of adding strength training to endurance training in female athletes. Heavy strength training did not improve running performance or economy compared to endurance training alone.

title: Antioxidant supplements and endurance exercise: Current evidence and mechanistic insights
authors: Shaun A. Mason, Adam J. Trewin, Lewan Parker, Glenn D. Wadley
abstract: This review examines antioxidant supplements for endurance athletes. Most supplements lack evidence for performance enhancement, with some potentially hindering training adaptations.

title: Effects of Endurance Training and Chlorogenic Acid on Oxidative and Nitrosative Stress Markers in Prediabetic Male Mice
authors: Sahar Ghasemi Pour, Sayyed M. Marandi
abstract: Endurance training and chlorogenic acid were studied for their effects on oxidative and nitrosative stress in prediabetic mice. Both interventions improved antioxidant capacity, with endurance training reducing glutathione and chlorogenic acid increasing total antioxidant capacity.

title: Effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on endogenous antioxidant systems and heat shock proteins in response to endurance training
authors: Kristoffer T. Cumming, Truls Raastad, Geir Holden, Nasser E. Bastani, Damaris Schneeberger, Maria Pa...
abstract: This study examined vitamin C and E supplementation's effects on antioxidant and heat shock protein systems during endurance training. Supplementation did not alter long-term training adaptations but increased acute exercise stress responses.

title: The effect of vitamin C on bronchoconstriction and respiratory symptoms caused by exercise: a review and statistical analysis
authors: Harri Hemilä
abstract: Vitamin C was studied for its effects on exercise-induced bronchoconstriction and respiratory symptoms. It significantly reduced post-exercise lung function decline and the incidence of respiratory symptoms.

title: Effects of intermittent sprint and plyometric training on endurance running performance
authors: Danny Lum, Frankie Tan, Joel Pang, Tiago M. Barbosa
source: Journal of Sport and Health Science
abstract: This study compared intermittent sprint and plyometric training in endurance runners. Both methods improved 10-km performance and peak power, with a correlation between running performance and relative peak power.

title: Effect of high-dose vitamin C and E supplementation on muscle recovery and training adaptation: a mini review
authors: Jooyoung Kim
abstract: This review examined high-dose vitamin C and E supplementation's effects on exercise-induced muscle recovery and training adaptation. Evidence suggests potential negative impacts on adaptation, with unclear benefits for recovery.

title: Performance and Submaximal Adaptations to Additional Speed-Endurance Training Vs. Continuous Moderate-Intensity Aerobic Training in Male Endurance Athletes
authors: Vincenzo Rago, Peter Krustrup, Magni Mohr
abstract: This study compared speed-endurance training (SET) with moderate-intensity training (MIT) in male endurance athletes. SET led to greater physiological demands and superior improvements in performance and running economy compared to MIT.

title: Human skeletal muscle ascorbate is highly responsive to changes in vitamin C intake and plasma concentrations 1 2 3
authors: Anitra C Carr, Stephanie M Bozonet, Juliet M Pullar, Jeremy W Simcock, Margreet CM Vissers
abstract: Skeletal muscle ascorbate levels were studied in response to vitamin C intake from kiwifruit. Muscle ascorbate concentrations significantly increased with intake and were more responsive than leukocytes.

title: Effects of exercise training with short‐duration intermittent hypoxia on endurance performance and muscle metabolism in well‐trained mice
authors: Junichi Suzuki
abstract: This study investigated the effects of intermittent hypoxia combined with exercise training on endurance in mice. Intermittent hypoxia enhanced endurance training and hybrid training by improving fatty acid and pyruvate oxidation.

title: Vitamin C Supplementation Slightly Improves Physical Activity Levels and Reduces Cold Incidence in Men with Marginal Vitamin C Status: A Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: Carol S. Johnston, Gillean M. Barkyoumb, Sara S. Schumacher
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C supplementation's effects on physical activity and colds in men with marginal vitamin C status. Supplementation slightly increased physical activity and reduced cold incidence and duration.

title: Effects of Plyometric Training on Explosive and Endurance Performance at Sea Level and at High Altitude
authors: David Cristóbal Andrade, Ana Rosa Beltrán, Cristian Labarca-Valenzuela, Oscar Manzo-Botarelli, Erwin...
abstract: A 4-week plyometric training program improved explosive and endurance performance at sea level. This training also enhanced performance at high altitude compared to a control group.

title: Vitamin C and glutathione supplementation: a review of their additive effects on exercise performance
authors: Eunjoo Lee, Hun-Young Park, Sung-Woo Kim, Jisu Kim, Kiwon Lim
abstract: This review examined vitamin C and glutathione supplementation's effects on exercise performance. Combined supplementation's additive effects are anticipated but remain largely unexplored and require further study.

title: Endurance training of respiratory muscles improves cycling performance in fit young cyclists
authors: Paige Holm, Angela Sattler, Ralph F Fregosi
abstract: Respiratory muscle endurance training was performed by fit cyclists. This training improved cycling performance and respiratory muscle endurance capacity.

title: Oligomerized lychee fruit extract (OLFE) and a mixture of vitamin C and vitamin E for endurance capacity in a double blind randomized controlled trial
authors: Seung Wan Kang, Seokyung Hahn, Jung-Kyu Kim, Seung-Min Yang, Byung-Joo Park, Sang Chul Lee
source: Journal of Clinical Biochemistry and Nutrition
abstract: Oligomerized lychee fruit extract (OLFE) and a vitamin C/E mixture were tested for endurance effects in exercising males. OLFE significantly improved running time and anaerobic threshold, while the vitamin mixture unexpectedly reduced VO2 max.

title: Temperate performance and metabolic adaptations following endurance training performed under environmental heat stress
authors: Ed Maunder, Daniel J. Plews, Gareth A. Wallis, Matthew J. Brick, Warren B. Leigh, Wee‐Leong Chang, C...
abstract: Endurance training in 33°C versus 18°C was studied in trained males. Training in heat improved time-trial performance and mitochondrial citrate synthase activity more than training in temperate conditions.

title: Performance-Related Physiological and Haematological Changes During Pregnancy and Postpartum in a Well-Trained Cyclist Performing Endurance Training
authors: Nicki Winfield Almquist, Øyvind Sandbakk, Guro Strøm Solli
abstract: This case study tracked physiological and hematological changes in a trained cyclist during pregnancy and postpartum. Hematological values increased during pregnancy without a corresponding VO2peak rise, but training helped restore VO2peak and improve power postpartum.

title: Effects of Acute Vitamin C plus Vitamin E Supplementation on Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage in Runners: A Double-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial
authors: María Martínez-Ferrán, Víctor Cuadrado-Peñafiel, Juan Manuel Sánchez-Andreo, Marta Villar-Lucas, Món...
abstract: This study investigated if vitamin C and E supplementation reduces exercise-induced muscle damage in runners. The supplementation did not significantly improve muscle damage markers or performance compared to a placebo.

title: Early morning run-training results in enhanced endurance performance adaptations in mice
authors: Stuart J. Hesketh, Casey L. Sexton, Christopher A. Wolff, Mark R. Viggars, Karyn A. Esser
abstract: Six weeks of endurance training in mice showed that morning training led to greater adaptation than afternoon training. This suggests morning exercise improves muscle clock alignment for better performance.

title: Vitamin C and E Supplementation Effects in Professional Soccer Players Under Regular Training
authors: Claudio C Zoppi, Rodrigo Hohl, Fernando C Silva, Fernanda L Lazarim, Joaquim MF Antunes Neto, Mirtes...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C and E supplementation in professional soccer players during training. Supplementation reduced lipid peroxidation and muscle damage but did not improve performance.

title: EFFECTS OF L-ASCORBIC ACID AND ALPHA-TOCOPHEROL ON BIOCHEMICAL PARAMETERS OF SWIMMING-INDUCED OXIDATIVE STRESS IN SERUM OF GUINEA PIGS
authors: Marija Bursać-Mitrović, Dragan R. Milovanović, Radoslav Mitić, Danijela Jovanović, Miroslav Sovrlić,...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of L-ascorbic acid and alpha-tocopherol on biochemical markers of oxidative stress in guinea pigs after swimming. The vitamins demonstrated protective antioxidant activity, with combined treatments showing a synergistic effect.

title: Effect of temperature on fatty acid metabolism in skeletal muscle mitochondria of untrained and endurance-trained rats
authors: Jerzy A. Zoladz, Agnieszka Koziel, Izabela Broniarek, Andrzej M. Woyda-Ploszczyca, Karolina Ogrodna,...
abstract: Skeletal muscle mitochondria from untrained and trained rats were studied at different temperatures to assess lipid fuel oxidation. Endurance training increased fatty acid oxidation capacity at all temperatures, with hyperthermia enhancing and hypothermia attenuating oxidation rates.

title: Alleviation of ascorbic acid-induced gastric high acidity by calcium ascorbate  in vitro  and  in vivo
authors: Joon-Kyung Lee, Sang-Hyuk Jung, Sang-Eun Lee, Joo-Hui Han, Eunji Jo, Hyun-Soo Park, Kyung-Sun Heo, D...
source: The Korean Journal of Physiology & Pharmacology : Official Journal of the Korean Physiological Society and the Korean Society of Pharmacology
abstract: This study compared calcium ascorbate and ascorbic acid's effects on gastric acidity and bioavailability. Calcium ascorbate increased gastric pH and plasma concentrations, suggesting it mitigates ascorbic acid's side effects.

title: Short-Term High-Dose Vitamin C and E Supplementation Attenuates Muscle Damage and Inflammatory Responses to Repeated Taekwondo Competitions: A Randomized Placebo-Controlled Trial
authors: Chun-Chung Chou, Yu-Chi Sung, Glen Davison, Chung-Yu Chen, Yi-Hung Liao
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on elite Taekwondo athletes. Supplementation attenuated muscle damage, hemolysis, and inflammatory responses to repeated competitions.

title: Can supplementation with vitamin C and E alter physiological adaptations to strength training?
authors: Gøran Paulsen, Kristoffer T Cumming, Håvard Hamarsland, Elisabet Børsheim, Sveinung Berntsen, Truls ...
source: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation
abstract: High doses of vitamins C and E were tested for their effects on strength training adaptations in young and older men. Supplementation blunted adaptations in young men but showed potential benefits in older men.

title: Effects of Exercise Training under Hyperbaric Oxygen on Oxidative Stress Markers and Endurance Performance in Young Soccer Players: A Pilot Study
authors: Carlos Burgos, Carlos Henríquez-Olguín, David Cristóbal Andrade, Rodrigo Ramírez-Campillo, Oscar F. ...
abstract: This pilot study investigated the effects of hyperbaric oxygen training on young soccer players. The training improved endurance performance without increasing oxidative stress markers.

title: Controversies of antioxidant vitamins supplementation in exercise: ergogenic or ergolytic effects in humans?
authors: Cainara Lins Draeger, Andréia Naves, Natália Marques, Ana Beatriz Baptistella, Renata Alves Carnauba...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This commentary reviews recent studies on antioxidant vitamin supplementation and exercise-induced oxidative stress. Findings are controversial, with supplementation showing ergogenic, ergolytic, or no effects on physiological parameters and antioxidant enzyme activity.

title: The effect of almond consumption on elements of endurance exercise performance in trained athletes
authors: Muqing Yi, Jinde Fu, Lili Zhou, Hong Gao, Chenguang Fan, Jing Shao, Baohua Xu, Qirong Wang, Juntao L...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study examined the effects of almond consumption on endurance exercise performance in trained athletes. Almonds improved cycling distance and enhanced carbohydrate utilization and oxygen efficiency during exercise compared to a placebo.

title: Changes in Endurance Performance in Young Athletes During Two Training Seasons
authors: Łukasz Tota, Marcin Maciejczyk, Ilona Pokora, Jerzy Cempla, Wanda Pilch, Tomasz Pałka
abstract: This study tracked endurance performance in young runners over two training seasons. While the first season improved maximal oxygen uptake, the second season enhanced running economy with similar training loads.

title: Vitamin C deficiency causes muscle atrophy and a deterioration in physical performance
authors: Shoko Takisawa, Tomoko Funakoshi, Tomofumi Yatsu, Kisaburo Nagata, Toshiro Aigaki, Shuichi Machida, ...
abstract: This study investigated the effects of vitamin C deficiency on skeletal muscle in mice. Vitamin C deficiency leads to muscle atrophy and reduced physical performance, which can be reversed with supplementation.

title: Exercise performance and physiological responses: the potential role of redox imbalance
authors: Kavey Vidal, Nathaniel Robinson, Stephen J. Ives
abstract: This study investigated the effects of hyperoxia and an antioxidant cocktail on cycling performance and physiological responses. Ingesting an antioxidant cocktail impaired performance, ventilation, and economy, suggesting a disruption of redox balance.

title: Prolonged Heat Acclimation and Aerobic Performance in Endurance Trained Athletes
authors: C. Jacob Mikkelsen, Nicklas Junge, Jacob F. Piil, Nathan B. Morris, Laura Oberholzer, Christoph Sieb...
abstract: This study investigated prolonged heat acclimation's effects on endurance cyclists' aerobic performance in cool conditions. Prolonged heat training did not improve aerobic power or time trial performance in cool weather compared to standard training.

title: Marginal Ascorbate Status (Hypovitaminosis C) Results in an Attenuated Response to Vitamin C Supplementation
authors: Anitra C. Carr, Juliet M. Pullar, Stephanie M. Bozonet, Margreet C. M. Vissers
abstract: This study analyzed vitamin C supplementation in individuals with low baseline levels. A 50 mg/day supplement was insufficient to restore adequate vitamin C status in these individuals.

title: Protein and the Adaptive Response With Endurance Training: Wishful Thinking or a Competitive Edge?
authors: Pim Knuiman, Maria T. E. Hopman, Conor Verbruggen, Marco Mensink
abstract: This perspective reviews the current evidence on protein's role in endurance training adaptations. While acute exercise may increase amino acid oxidation, the impact of dietary protein on endurance performance remains largely unproven.

title: Protective Role of Vitamin C Intake on Muscle Damage in Male Adolescents Performing Strenuous Physical Activity
authors: Shreef G. N. Gabrial, Marie-Christine R. Shakib, Gamal N. Gabrial
source: Open Access Macedonian Journal of Medical Sciences
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C's effect on muscle damage in male adolescents during strenuous exercise. Vitamin C supplementation significantly reduced markers of muscle damage, oxidative stress, and inflammation.

title: Degradation of Patulin in Pear Juice and Apple Juice by Ascorbic Acid and the Combination of Ascorbic Acid and Ferrous Iron
authors: Xiaoyan Wei, Mengyao Du, Sung-Yong Hong, Ae-Son Om
abstract: Ascorbic acid and its combination with ferrous iron were tested for patulin degradation in pear and apple juices. Ascorbic acid alone degraded patulin effectively, with the combination showing even higher degradation rates.

title: Targeted Metabolomics in High Performance Sports: Differences between the Resting Metabolic Profile of Endurance- and Strength-Trained Athletes in Comparison with Sedentary Subjects over the Course of a Training Year
authors: Mario Parstorfer, Gernot Poschet, Dorothea Kronsteiner, Kirsten Brüning, Birgit Friedmann-Bette
abstract: This study compared the resting metabolic profiles of endurance athletes, strength athletes, and sedentary individuals across a training year. Differences were found between groups, with specific metabolites varying throughout the year, particularly in strength athletes.

title: Potential harms of supplementation with high doses of antioxidants in athletes
authors: Shunchang Li, Babatunde Fasipe, Ismail Laher
abstract: This paper reviews the use of high-dose antioxidant supplements by athletes. It concludes that these supplements may hinder beneficial training adaptations and potentially cause harm.

title: Influence of Interval Training Frequency on Time-Trial Performance in Elite Endurance Athletes
authors: Espen Tønnessen, Jonny Hisdal, Bent R. Ronnestad
source: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
abstract: This study compared the effects of four short versus two longer interval training sessions weekly in elite endurance athletes. Two longer sessions per week led to greater improvements in time-trial performance and physiological adaptations than four shorter sessions.

title: Do Antioxidant Vitamins Prevent Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage? A Systematic Review
authors: María Martinez-Ferran, Fabian Sanchis-Gomar, Carl J. Lavie, Giuseppe Lippi, Helios Pareja-Galeano
abstract: This systematic review examined vitamin C and E supplementation's effects on exercise-induced muscle damage. The available data are not conclusive regarding whether these vitamins prevent muscle damage.

title: Enhancing Supplemental Effects of Acute Natural Antioxidant Derived from Yeast Fermentation and Vitamin C on Sports Performance in Triathlon Athletes: A Randomized, Double-Blinded, Placebo-Controlled, Crossover Trial
authors: Eunjoo Lee, Hun-Young Park, Sung-Woo Kim, Yerin Sun, Jae-Ho Choi, Jisoo Seo, Yanghoon Peter Jung, Ah...
abstract: This study examined the effects of combined vitamin C and glutathione supplementation on middle-aged triathletes during exercise. The combination improved metabolic, skeletal muscle oxygenation, cardiac, and antioxidant functions compared to individual supplements or placebo.

title: The Effect of Two Speed Endurance Training Regimes on Performance of Soccer Players
authors: F. Marcello Iaia, Matteo Fiorenza, Enrico Perri, Giampietro Alberti, Grégoire P. Millet, Jens Bangsb...
abstract: Two speed endurance training regimes were compared in young male soccer players. SEP training improved repeated sprint and intermittent exercise performance, while SEM training enhanced fatigue tolerance and speed maintenance.

title: The Effect of Vitamin C and E Supplementation on Muscle Damage and Oxidative Stress in Female Athletes: A Clinical Trial
authors: Maryam Taghiyar, Leila Darvishi, Gholamrez Askari, Awat Feizi, Mitra Hariri, Nafiseh Shokri Mashhadi...
abstract: This study investigated vitamin C and E supplementation's effects on muscle damage and oxidative stress in female athletes. Results showed vitamin C and E supplementation reduced muscle damage and oxidative stress markers.

title: Upper-Body Muscular Endurance Training Improves Performance Following 50 min of Double Poling in Well-Trained Cross-Country Skiers
authors: Jørgen Børve, Steffen N. Jevne, Bjarne Rud, Thomas Losnegard
abstract: Upper-body muscular endurance training was added to standard training for cross-country skiers. This training improved double poling performance and reduced oxygen cost during prolonged effort.

title: The Effect of Vitamins C and E Supplementation on Muscle Damage, Performance, and Body Composition in Athlete Women: A Clinical Trial
authors: Maryam Taghiyar, Reza Ghiasvand, Gholamreza Askari, Awat Feizi, Mitra Hariri, Nafiseh Shokri Mashhad...
abstract: This clinical trial examined the effects of vitamin C and E supplementation on muscle damage, performance, and body composition in trained female athletes over four weeks. The study found no significant improvements in any of these parameters due to the supplementation.

title: Sustained Endurance Training Leads to Metabolomic Adaptation
authors: Astrid Weiss, Katharina Alack, Stephan Klatt, Sven Zukunft, Ralph Schermuly, Torsten Frech, Frank-Ch...
abstract: This study compared the metabolomic profiles of endurance-trained and untrained individuals. Endurance training leads to distinct changes in phospholipids, acylcarnitines, bile acids, and polyunsaturated fatty acids at rest.

title: Prior exercise and antioxidant supplementation: effect on oxidative stress and muscle injury
authors: Richard J Bloomer, Michael J Falvo, Brian K Schilling, Webb A Smith
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: This study investigated the effects of prior eccentric exercise and antioxidant supplementation on muscle injury and oxidative stress in resistance-trained men. Neither intervention, alone or combined, significantly reduced markers of muscle injury or oxidative stress.

title: Six Sessions of Sprint-Interval Training Did Not Improve Endurance and Neuromuscular Performance in Untrained Men
authors: Raphael Bertschinger, Louis-Solal Giboin, Markus Gruber
abstract: Six sessions of sprint-interval training were administered to untrained men to assess endurance and neuromuscular performance. The training did not improve endurance or neuromuscular function compared to a control group.

title: The Road to Gold: Training and Peaking Characteristics in the Year Prior to a Gold Medal Endurance Performance
authors: Espen Tønnessen, Øystein Sylta, Thomas A. Haugen, Erlend Hem, Ida S. Svendsen, Stephen Seiler
abstract: Elite endurance athletes trained approximately 800 hours annually, with 90% at low intensity. Training volume decreased before peaking, but high-intensity training remained stable, and tapering did not align with experimental recommendations.

title: Acute vitamin C improves cardiac function, not exercise capacity, in adults with type 2 diabetes
authors: Rebecca L. Scalzo, Timothy A. Bauer, Kylie Harrall, Kerrie Moreau, Cemal Ozemek, Leah Herlache, Shaw...
abstract: Acute vitamin C infusion was studied in adults with type 2 diabetes and healthy adults. Vitamin C improved diastolic cardiac function but did not affect exercise capacity or other measures of vascular function.

title: Performance-related physiological changes induced by one year of endurance training in young athletes
authors: Christina Mishica, Heikki Kyröläinen, Maarit Valtonen, Hans-Christer Holmberg, Vesa Linnamo
source: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
abstract: Endurance training was studied in young cross-country skiers over one year. Ski-specific performance improved significantly, but maximal oxygen uptake did not, suggesting upper-body power was key.

title: Vitamin C and E Treatment Blunts Sprint Interval Training–Induced Changes in Inflammatory Mediator-, Calcium-, and Mitochondria-Related Signaling in Recreationally Active Elderly Humans
authors: Victoria L. Wyckelsma, Tomas Venckunas, Marius Brazaitis, Stefano Gastaldello, Audrius Snieckus, Ner...
abstract: Sprint interval training in elderly individuals was studied with and without antioxidant treatment. Antioxidants blunted training-induced cellular signaling changes in muscle, but did not affect performance outcomes.

title: The effects of antioxidant vitamin supplementation on resistance exercise induced lipid peroxidation in trained and untrained participants
authors: Peter E Viitala, Ian J Newhouse, Norm LaVoie, Christine Gottardo
abstract: This study investigated the impact of vitamin E supplementation on exercise-induced lipid peroxidation in trained and untrained individuals. Vitamin E supplementation did not reduce oxidative damage, and training status did not affect lipid peroxidation levels post-exercise.

title: Active Recovery Induces Greater Endurance Adaptations When Performing Sprint Interval Training
authors: Takaki Yamagishi, John Babraj
source: Journal of Strength and Conditioning Research
abstract: This study compared the effects of active versus passive recovery during sprint interval training. Active recovery during SIT led to greater improvements in critical power and a tendency for increased maximal power output.

title: Improved exercise performance and increased aerobic capacity after endurance training of patients with stable polymyositis and dermatomyositis
authors: Li Alemo Munters, Maryam Dastmalchi, Abram Katz, Mona Esbjörnsson, Ingela Loell, Balsam Hanna, Maria...
abstract: This study investigated endurance training in patients with polymyositis or dermatomyositis. Endurance training improved exercise performance and aerobic capacity, with some patients also showing clinical improvement.

title: Effects of Vitamin C Supplementation on Plasma and Urinary Vitamin C Concentration in Korean Women
authors: Jayoung Choi, Do-Yeon Kim, Ryowon Choue, Hyunjung Lim
abstract: This study investigated the effects of 100 mg and 2,000 mg vitamin C supplements on Korean women. Both doses increased plasma and urinary vitamin C, with the higher dose reducing oxidative stress and the lower dose reducing fatigue.

title: Frequency and perceived influence of menopausal symptoms on training and performance in female endurance athletes
authors: Heather M. Hamilton *, Natalie M. Yarish, Kristin E. Heron
abstract: This study surveyed 187 female endurance athletes aged 40-60 about menopausal symptoms. A high frequency of symptoms was reported, with joint/muscular discomfort, weight gain, and sleep problems most negatively impacting training and performance.

title: Differences in the Pro/Antioxidative Status and Cellular Stress Response in Elderly Women after 6 Weeks of Exercise Training Supported by 1000 mg of Vitamin C Supplementation
authors: Małgorzata Żychowska, Ewa Sadowska-Krępa, Elisabetta Damiani, Luca Tiano, Ewa Ziemann, Alicja Nowak-...
abstract: This study examined the effects of exercise training with vitamin C supplementation on antioxidant status and cellular stress response in elderly women. Vitamin C supplementation increased oxidative stress markers and influenced minor changes in gene expression related to training adaptation.

title: The Effects of Strength Training Combined with Vitamin C and E Supplementation on Skeletal Muscle Mass and Strength: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
authors: Maurilio T. Dutra, Wagner Rodrigues Martins, Alexandre L. A. Ribeiro, Martim Bottaro
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis examined studies on vitamin C and E supplementation combined with strength training. The findings suggest these supplements do not enhance muscle strength or mass and may even attenuate hypertrophy.

title: Mindfulness Training Enhances Endurance Performance and Executive Functions in Athletes: An Event-Related Potential Study
authors: Jui-Ti Nien, Chih-Han Wu, Kao-Teng Yang, Yu-Min Cho, Chien-Heng Chu, Yu-Kai Chang, Chenglin Zhou
abstract: A five-week mindfulness program was tested on university athletes. The training improved endurance, executive functions, and reduced neural conflict monitoring.

title: Vitamin C and E supplementation does not affect heat shock proteins or endogenous antioxidants in trained skeletal muscles during 12 weeks of strength training
authors: K. T. Cumming, T. Raastad, A. Sørstrøm, M. P. Paronetto, N. Mercatelli, I. Ugelstad, D. Caporossi, G...
abstract: This study examined the impact of vitamin C and E supplementation on trained individuals undergoing strength training. The supplementation did not alter acute exercise stress responses or long-term adaptations in heat shock proteins or endogenous antioxidants.

title: Nicotinic Acid Improves Endurance Performance of Mice Subjected to Treadmill Exercise
authors: Robert Ringseis, Denise K. Gessner, Anna M. Beer, Yvonne Albrecht, Gaiping Wen, Erika Most, Karsten ...
abstract: This study investigated the effect of a high nicotinic acid diet combined with treadmill exercise on mouse endurance performance. The combined treatment significantly improved endurance and altered muscle fiber composition compared to exercise alone or control.

title: Acclimation Training Improves Endurance Cycling Performance in the Heat without Inducing Endotoxemia
authors: Joshua H. Guy, David B. Pyne, Glen B. Deakin, Catherine M. Miller, Andrew M. Edwards
abstract: This study investigated the effects of short-term heat training on endurance cycling performance and immune responses. Heat training improved cycling performance without causing significant immune system challenges.

title: Oral vitamin C restores endothelial function during acute inflammation in young and older adults
authors: Elizabeth C. Lefferts, Brooks A. Hibner, Wesley K. Lefferts, Natalia S. Lima, Tracy Baynard, Jacob M...
abstract: Oral vitamin C was given to young and older adults during acute inflammation to assess its effect on vascular function. Vitamin C restored endothelial function, but not aortic stiffness, during inflammation.

title: An 8-week exergame-based exercise training program improves cardiovascular endurance, muscular strength and endurance performances among primary school children in Taiwan
authors: Chi-Fang Lin, Po-Fu Lee, Yan-Jhu Su, I-Tung Lin, Hsiao-Fang Kao, Yi-Chuan Hung, Mei-Ling Chao, Chien...
abstract: An 8-week exergame program was tested on Taiwanese primary school children. The program significantly improved cardiovascular endurance and muscular strength/endurance compared to a control group.

title: Exercise Training and Vitamin C Supplementation Affects Ferritin mRNA in Leukocytes without Affecting Prooxidative/Antioxidative Balance in Elderly Women
authors: Małgorzata Żychowska, Agata Grzybkowska, Monika Wiech, Robert Urbański, Wanda Pilch, Anna Piotrowska...
abstract: Exercise training with vitamin C supplementation decreased ferritin mRNA in elderly women's leukocytes. This intervention did not alter the prooxidative/antioxidative balance.

title: Effects of blood flow restriction training on aerobic capacity and performance in endurance athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
authors: Zekai Zhang, Xuejiao Gao, Lang Gao
source: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation
abstract: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluated blood flow restriction (BFR) training's effects on endurance athletes. BFR training moderately improves aerobic capacity and endurance performance, and significantly enhances muscle strength.

title: International Society of Sports Nutrition position stand: effects of dietary antioxidants on exercise and sports performance
authors: Drew E. Gonzalez; Broderick L. Dickerson; Brandon M. Roberts; Jennifer A. Kurtz; Hunter S. Waldman; ...
source: Journal of the International Society of Sports Nutrition
abstract: Following a comprehensive review, the International Society of Sports Nutrition (ISSN) has developed an official position on the role of dietary antioxidants in exercise and sport. Antioxidants play a

title: ON THE INACTIVATION OF ASCORBIC ACID OXIDASE
authors: Wendell H. Powers, Charles R. Dawson
abstract: Ascorbic acid oxidase is rapidly inactivated during ascorbic acid oxidation, with inactivation partly due to environmental factors and partly inherent to the system. Protective agents like catalase and peroxidase significantly reduce this inactivation without affecting the reaction rate.

title: Supplementation with Vitamins C and E and Exercise-Induced Delayed-Onset Muscle Soreness: A Systematic Review
authors: María F. Torre, María Martinez-Ferran, Néstor Vallecillo, Sergio L. Jiménez, Carlos Romero-Morales, ...
abstract: This systematic review examined vitamin C and E supplementation's effect on exercise-induced muscle soreness. The evidence is insufficient to confirm these vitamins minimize delayed-onset muscle soreness.

title: Elevated hepcidin serum level in response to inflammatory and iron signals in exercising athletes is independent of moderate supplementation with vitamin C and E
authors: Víctor Díaz, Ana B Peinado, Laura Barba-Moreno, Sandro Altamura, Javier Butragueño, Marcela González...
abstract: This study investigated hepcidin levels in athletes after exercise. Hepcidin remained elevated despite vitamin C and E supplementation, indicating these vitamins do not alter the response to inflammatory and iron signals.

title: Membrane Permeabilities of Ascorbic Acid and Ascorbate
authors: Christof Hannesschlaeger, Peter Pohl
abstract: This study investigated the membrane permeability of ascorbic acid and ascorbate. Ascorbate permeability is negligible, with transport occurring via protonation/deprotonation, suggesting passive transport is insufficient for vitamin C uptake.

title: Repeated Inhalation of Peppermint Essential Oil Improves Exercise Performance in Endurance-Trained Rats
authors: Wei Zhang, Rongpei Shi, Tian Gao, Yang Hu, Jiaheng Zhou, Chenhan Li, Panpan Wang, Hongyan Yang, Wenj...
abstract: Repeated inhalation of peppermint essential oil was studied in endurance-trained rats. The oil significantly improved exercise performance and reduced oxidative damage, enhancing training effects.

title: Vitamin C Is Essential for the Maintenance of Skeletal Muscle Functions
authors: Shoko Takisawa, Yuka Takino, Jaewon Lee, Shuichi Machida, Akihito Ishigami
abstract: Long-term vitamin C deficiency was studied in male mice lacking VC synthesis, showing muscle atrophy and reduced physical ability. Vitamin C is essential for maintaining skeletal muscle function in both sexes.

title: Adaptations to strength training differ between endurance-trained and untrained women
authors: Olav Vikmoen, Truls Raastad, Stian Ellefsen, Bent R. Rønnestad
abstract: Endurance-trained and untrained women underwent 11 weeks of strength training. Concurrent training did not impair strength or hypertrophy gains, but attenuated increases in explosive power.

title: Can vitamin C supplementation reverse the effects of exercise training in polluted air on oxidative stress markers? A randomized controlled trial
authors: Amin Eatemadyboroujeni, Mehdi Kargarfard, Hojatollah Alaei
abstract: This study investigated the effects of exercise, polluted air, and vitamin C on oxidative stress markers in rats. Vitamin C supplementation did not significantly reverse the increased oxidative stress caused by exercise in polluted air.

title: Endurance Training Protocol and Longitudinal Performance Assays for  Drosophila melanogaster
authors: Martin J. Tinkerhess, Sara Ginzberg, Nicole Piazza, Robert J. Wessells
abstract: A novel apparatus, the Power Tower, was developed for large-scale endurance training of fruit flies. This system allows for simultaneous training of many flies and tracking of their performance over time.

title: Antioxidant Vitamin C Prevents Decline in Endothelial Function during Sitting
authors: Saurabh S. Thosar, Sylvanna L. Bielko, Chad S. Wiggins, James E. Klaunig, Kieren J. Mather, Janet P....
abstract: This study investigated if Vitamin C prevents endothelial function decline during prolonged sitting. Vitamin C supplementation prevented the impairment of femoral artery dilation after three hours of sitting.

title: CYP1A2  Genotype and the Ergogenic Effect of Acute Caffeine Intake on Muscular Strength and Endurance Performance in Trained Individuals
authors: Juan Jesús Montalvo‐Alonso, Marta del Val‐Manzano, Iván Martín‐Rivas, Carmen Ferragut, David Valadés...
source: Scandinavian Journal of Medicine & Science in Sports
abstract: This study investigated if CYP1A2 genotype affects caffeine's ergogenic impact on strength and endurance in trained individuals. Caffeine improved performance, with benefits greatest in AA, intermediate in AC, and minimal in CC genotype carriers.

title: Antioxidants and Exercise: A Redox-Informed Framework for Training Adaptation, Performance, and Recovery
authors: Dan Cristian Mănescu; Andrei Tudor; Andreea Maria Mănescu; Iulius Radulian Mărgărit; Cătălin Octavia...
abstract: Antioxidants can hinder training adaptations by blunting exercise-induced signals. However, certain food-derived antioxidants may aid recovery without impairing gains. A framework called Redox-Adaptive Periodization is proposed to optimize antioxidant use based on training goals.

title: Acute Physiological and Thermoregulatory Responses to Extended Interval Training in Endurance Runners: Influence of Athletic Performance and Age
authors: Felipe García-Pinillos, Víctor Manuel Soto-Hermoso, Pedro Ángel Latorre-Román
abstract: This study examined the physiological and thermoregulatory responses of endurance runners to extended interval training. No significant differences were found based on athletic performance or age, suggesting similar responses at comparable relative intensities.

title: The Role of Vitamin C in Two Distinct Physiological States: Physical Activity and Sleep
authors: Aneta Otocka-Kmiecik, Aleksandra Król
abstract: This paper reviews the relationship between vitamin C, physical activity, and sleep. Vitamin C supplementation may benefit sleep health and aspects of physical activity, potentially by influencing oxidative stress.

title: Effects of Endurance and Endurance–Strength Training on Endothelial Function in Women with Obesity: A Randomized Trial
authors: Marzena Ratajczak, Damian Skrypnik, Paweł Bogdański, Edyta Mądry, Jarosław Walkowiak, Monika Szulińs...
source: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
abstract: This study compared endurance and combined endurance-strength training in obese women. Endurance training alone improved endothelial function markers, while both improved lipid metabolism.

title: Vitamin C—Sources, Physiological Role, Kinetics, Deficiency, Use, Toxicity, and Determination
authors: Martin Doseděl, Eduard Jirkovský, Kateřina Macáková, Lenka Kujovská Krčmová, Lenka Javorská, Jana Po...
abstract: This review discusses vitamin C's broad physiological roles beyond its antioxidant function, including its impact on iron absorption and epigenetic processes. While essential for preventing scurvy, high doses can be pro-oxidant and potentially harmful, with limited proven benefits for other diseases.

title: The Effect of Antioxidant Supplementation on Fatigue during Exercise: Potential Role for NAD + (H)
authors: John Mach, Adrian W. Midgley, Steve Dank, Ross S. Grant, David J. Bentley
abstract: This study investigated the impact of antioxidant supplementation on exercise fatigue and NAD+ levels. Antioxidant supplementation increased exercise time to fatigue and serum NAD+ levels, suggesting reduced oxidative stress improved aerobic respiration.

title: Influence of endurance and endurance–strength training on mineral status in women with abdominal obesity: a randomized trial
authors: Damian Skrypnik, Paweł Bogdański, Katarzyna Skrypnik, Edyta Mądry, Joanna Karolkiewicz, Monika Szuli...
abstract: Endurance and endurance-strength training were compared in abdominally obese women. Endurance-strength training showed more favorable effects on mineral balance, particularly for iron, magnesium, zinc, and copper.

title: Ascorbic Acid Alleviates Water Stress in Young Peach Trees and Improves Their Performance after Rewatering
authors: Consuelo Penella, Ángeles Calatayud, Juan C. Melgar
abstract: Ascorbic acid was applied to young peach trees to study its effect on water stress tolerance. Ascorbic acid improved physiological recovery and reduced cell damage in water-stressed trees, suggesting its potential as a management tool.

title: Antioxidant Supplementation Impairs Changes in Body Composition Induced by Strength Training in Young Women
authors: MAURILIO T. DUTRA, SÁVIO ALEX, ALYSON F. SILVA, LEE E. BROWN, MARTIM BOTTARO
abstract: This study examined the effects of strength training with antioxidant supplementation on body composition in young women. Antioxidant supplementation impaired strength training-induced gains in fat-free mass and reductions in fat mass.
